questionText:

"On 15 August 1947, as festivities erupted in New Delhi to celebrate Indian independence, Mahatma Gandhi was in Calcutta, staying in an abandoned Muslim mansion (Hydari Mansion in Beliaghata). Admiring his moral courage, Viceroy Lord Mountbatten wrote to him: 'In the Punjab we have 55,000 soldiers and large-scale riots on our hands; in Bengal our force consists of one man, and there is no rioting.
